A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OBS-Diff and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The original scientific content can be matched reliably, including material displaced by v3's additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning experiments, generation-quality measurements, timing results and ablations in Section 5, with further DDPM and robustness results in Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the text-to-image comparisons, DDPM experiments, ablations and robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same timestep-aware Hessian, module-package calibration, sparsity procedures and attention-head rank fusion. Appendix C.3's DDPM adaptation is also unchanged; Appendix F proposes future extensions without introducing an implemented component.

E1.justification: The GCC3M/MS-COCO text-to-image coverage, CIFAR-10 DDPM task and Appendix D test scenarios are unchanged. Language, video and other applications mentioned in new Appendix F are prospective and are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Magnitude, Wanda and DSnoT, the EcoDiff/L1-norm structured comparisons, and Random Pruning, Magnitude Pruning and Diff-Pruning on DDPM. Changes to citation-year suffixes do not identify different methods.

E3.justification: Both retain the same metrics, model configurations, sparsities, 5K-prompt main evaluation, 1K-prompt ablation/robustness evaluations and 100 calibration prompts. The timing setup, robustness settings and DDPM 100K-step fine-tuning and 100-DDIM-step evaluation also match.

E4.justification: The timestep-weighting, package-count and calibration-size ablations are unchanged, as are Appendix D's guidance-scale, sampling-step, solver and calibration-distribution analyses. The new Appendix E paragraph summarizes existing qualitative figures rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or adds confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-14 and Figures 1-11 retain their numerical and qualitative results. For example, Table 1's SD3-Medium 50% OBS-Diff results remain 27.20 FID, 0.3167 CLIP and 0.6468 ImageReward; Table 10's OBS-Diff DDPM FID remains 7.55.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8 and their mathematical explanations are unchanged. Appendix F's statements about transferability provide no new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free one-shot pruning, multiple sparsity granularities, timestep-aware Hessians, grouped calibration and state-of-the-art performance. The added applications are framed as future work.

C2.justification: New Appendix F argues for transferability to additional diffusion, vision-language, reasoning and multimodal architectures, and compatibility with token merging, sparse attention and other compression techniques. This adds prospective applicability discussion; existing interpretations of experimental results and resource tradeoffs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same calibration details, baseline adaptations, package settings, hardware disclosures and computational information. The repository link is unchanged, with no additional reproduction instructions or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Appendix F substantially broadens the cited research context to diffusion language/video models, biomolecular diffusion, vision-language and reasoning models, and complementary acceleration techniques. The introduction adds general pruning references, while Section 2 and the bibliography remove SparseSSM. This is a broad literature and prospective-positioning expansion.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgements, an introductory paragraph in Appendix E and Appendix F, while lightly editing the introduction and related work. The header changes from Preprint to Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026; the existing scientific narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables retain their designs, with spacing and placement changes; Table 4 moves from PDF page 8 to page 9. Appendix F opens on page 18 but continues on page 22 after the retained qualitative figure pages.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens bibliographic context and adds prospective applications, but its method, mathematical content, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The Appendix E overview summarizes retained figures, and the editorial/layout changes provide no material net improvement or deterioration in clarity. Overall scientific quality remains essentially the same.
